Protocol amended to v1.1 before any screening decision: the blind dual-screen sample is 20% of each batch, minimum 50 and now capped at 150 records. Rationale: the first database run (IEEE Xplore, pillar 1) returned 3,759 records; 150 blind records give a kappa estimate with a confidence interval of roughly plus or minus 0.12, which is sufficient to apply the kappa 0.6 suspension rule, while 752 would make the AI-assistance policy more expensive than screening by hand. Sample drawn with a fixed seed as a prefix of the original 20% draw.

Protocol v1.2 after the first calibration round (IEEE pillar 1, 150 blind records): maintainer vs AI agreement was kappa -0.09, caused by two unwritten rules the maintainer applied (application-domain filter; coordination papers as in-scope) rather than by random disagreement. Criteria clarified: domain is not a criterion; coordination papers are E1 unless they contribute safety evaluation over multi-agent state; E2/E3 confirmed as hard excludes. The AI labels (prompt ta-screen-v1) already applied these rules and stand. Recalibration uses a fresh 50-record blind sample (protocol floor) because of maintainer time constraints; the first-round decisions are kept in decisions.csv as the calibration round.

Protocol v1.3: title/abstract screening becomes AI-first with maintainer review of every AI inclusion and a 5% (min 100) leak check of AI exclusions, replacing blind dual-screening with kappa. Reason: a second calibration round on the IEEE pillar-1 batch gave kappa 0.08 with the same systematic pattern as the first, and blind screening at this volume is not sustainable for a single maintainer. Both calibration rounds are retained in decisions.csv.

First database search run begun: IEEE Xplore, pillar 1, 3,760 records identified. Title/abstract stage complete under protocol v1.3 (AI-first, maintainer review of every inclusion): 937 records to full text, 2,823 excluded, leak check 0/135. Live PRISMA flow and per-batch screening table on the PRISMA-S page; raw exports, normalised records, AI labels and every decision published under data/. Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex runs for pillar 1, and the full-text stage, follow.

Protocol v1.4: full-text stage defined. Rule filters applied to the 936 IEEE pillar-1 records passing title/abstract: 9 excluded E3 (survey/magazine/book chapter), 2 excluded E5 (joint conference/journal publication). The remaining 925 are queued by a published tier rule: Tier A 344 (runtime inter-agent safety mechanism, 2022 or later, or LLM-agent setting), Tier B 203, Tier C 378. AI may draft extraction notes from full text; the maintainer makes every decision and score. Tiers are released as completed.

First papers enter the review from a database search: 11 of the first 12 Tier A full texts from the IEEE Xplore pillar-1 run included, 1 excluded E1. Full texts read from arXiv preprints; AI-drafted extraction notes (prompt ft-extract-v1, published under data/screening/prompts/) reviewed and every decision and score confirmed by the maintainer. 94 of 344 Tier A records have arXiv versions and are read first; the remainder need publisher PDFs.

Protocol v1.5: full-text inclusion criteria clarified after the first batches. Criterion (a) is strictly runtime (a mechanism that can override, veto, halt or defer at execution time); criterion (c) requires the multi-agent safety property to be the primary claim and measured outcome, so learned safety certificates and detectors qualify and navigation planners with collision constraints do not; minimum evaluation is one quantitative safety metric plus a baseline or ablation. Every included paper now carries a runtime_interceptor tag. The 39 drafted but undecided Tier A notes were re-tagged from their recorded flags (16 recommendations changed, all toward exclusion); the 12 decided records were unaffected. Extraction prompt ft-extract-v2.

Second and third full-text batches (IEEE pillar 1, Tier A, 39 records) decided under protocol v1.5: 16 included, 23 excluded. 51 of 93 open-access Tier A records now decided; 27 included from search in total.

Tier A open-access full texts complete for the IEEE pillar-1 run: all 93 Tier A records with an arXiv version decided (46 included, 47 excluded: 24 E1, 21 E2, 2 E4). Review grows to 73 papers, 46 from search. Remaining Tier A (251) and Tier B/C require publisher PDFs or a second abstract-level decision; the queue records open-access copies found via OpenAlex for 77 Tier B records.

Tier B records with arXiv versions decided (50): 13 included, 37 excluded (24 E1, 10 E2, 2 E4, 1 E6). Gap-matrix column definitions published; cross-domain evaluation tag removed from three papers evaluated in two robotics settings only. Review: 86 papers, 59 from search.

Three Tier B records read from repository copies decided. All records readable without publisher access are now decided for the IEEE pillar-1 run: 149 of 925 queued (A 93, B 56); the rest await publisher PDFs.

Second-pass title/abstract screening (ta-screen-v2, protocol v1.5 criteria) of the 779 IEEE pillar-1 records without open-access full text: 224 confirmed by the maintainer for publisher-copy request (Tier A 90, B 32, C 102), 555 excluded (494 E1, 46 E2, 14 E4, 1 E3); leak check 0 of 100. PRISMA flow now counts second-pass exclusions at the title/abstract stage.

Protocol v1.6: the full-text evaluation floor is judged against the claim a paper makes. Safety-mechanism papers still need a quantitative safety metric with a baseline or ablation; world-model and predictor papers need a predictive-accuracy metric with a baseline or ablation and enter as method evidence only, capped at RQ5 2. Reason: a predictor has no hazard rate to report, and the v1.5 wording would have excluded the representation-learning literature underpinning pillar 2.

Second database searched: the ACM Digital Library pillar-1 run adds 355 records (353 unique, 5 already in the review from IEEE Xplore or the API searches), of which 348 were screened on title and abstract and 60 sent to full text. Screening used a new first-pass prompt, ta-screen-v3, that applies the protocol v1.5 criteria directly, so records identified after v1.5 are judged once rather than screened in under the earlier criteria and out again at a second pass. 247 of the 288 exclusions are E1 off-topic, almost all multi-agent path-finding and coordination planners failing the primacy test on criterion (c). All 224 requested IEEE publisher full texts have been obtained bar one and their extraction notes drafted for maintainer review.
